newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end strong on telecoms, Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end strong on telecoms, Wall Street.

text.p: Brazilian stocks ended strongly up in heavy trade, pulled higher by the telecommunications sector and firm U.S. share prices, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 48 most liquid shares rose 189 points, or 1.8 percent, to close at 10,681 points. Volume totalled 651.6 million reais ($614.7 million).

Telecom stocks, led by bellwether Telebras and Telesp, closed firm as investors remained upbeat that a new telecommunications law setting the rules for the sale of the sector will pass Congress in the coming months.
"We noted a great demand for Telebras and Telesp," said a senior trader.

They said expectations of higher premiums on the Band B cellular bidding process and Telebras' stronger first quarter earnings, which analysts say will be released any time soon, also lifted the stocks higher.
Benchmark Telebras preferred gained 2.78 percent to end at 136.70 reais, while the preferred stock of Telesp, the first Telebras unit due to privatized, closed up 3.38 percent at 336 reais.
Other blue-chips also ended the session with strong rises, 2.34 percent, closing at 25 reais.

Traders said CVRD share prices continued to reflect uncertainties about the company under the new management. Control of CVRD was bought by a group led by private steelmaker CSN, whose share closed off 0.79 percent at 37.60 reais. After the market's close, CSN issued a statement with its first quarter earnings. The company closed the period with a net profit of 71.6 million reais, up 69 percent from the same period last year.

Banespa shares surged 15.97 percent, ending at 13.80 reais, on positive prospects for the bank as the federal government and Sao Paulo state finalize details on a debt restructuring deal sealed early this year.
Analysts said the market could continue advancing Tuesday on firmer telecoms stocks, but they noted an expected and, for some healthy, wave of profit-taking could reduce market gains.
